title: Understanding the Role of Reasoning Data in Pretraining
abstract: arXiv:2611.19042v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reasoning data expose models to multi-step reasoning, but reasoning traces may cover only a subset of the available facts. How should pretraining balance atomic facts with reasoning traces? We study this question by constructing a setting in which every fact provides an atomic training signal, while only a subset appears in reasoning supervision, enabling us to measure generalization to transitions observed atomically but never used in training traces. For a linear transformer, we derive the weight assigned to atomic training signals that minimizes held-transition squared error and show that its leading-order optimum increases with reasoning-chain length and decreases with the fraction of facts held out from reasoning traces. These trends persist in a full transformer layer with an MLP, softmax attention, and cross-entropy loss. translated_title: 理解推理数据在预训练中的作用
translated_abstract: 推理数据让模型接触多步推理过程，但推理轨迹可能只覆盖了可用事实的一部分。预训练应如何在原子事实与推理轨迹之间取得平衡？我们通过构建一个设定来研究这个问题：在该设定中，每个事实都提供原子训练信号，而只有其中一部分事实出现在推理监督中，这使我们能够衡量模型对那些以原子方式观察到、但从未在训练轨迹中使用的状态转移的泛化能力。对于线性 transformer，我们推导出了能最小化留出转移平方误差的原子训练信号权重，并证明其主导阶最优值随推理链长度增加而上升，随推理轨迹中留出的事实比例增加而下降。这些趋势在包含 MLP、softmax 注意力和交叉熵损失的完整 transformer 层中依然存在。我们进一步在两个自然语言设定中验证了推理复杂度与数据覆盖率的作用。
tldr: 该论文从理论与实验上研究了预训练中原子事实与推理轨迹的最优平衡，发现原子训练信号的最优权重随推理链长度增加而上升、随推理轨迹未覆盖的事实比例增加而下降。
en_tdlr: This paper theoretically and empirically studies how pretraining should balance atomic facts with reasoning traces, showing that the optimal weight on atomic training signals increases with reasoning-chain length and decreases with the fraction of facts held out from reasoning traces.
